cards.a: A VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) creates multiple isolated routing tables on one router, each with its own RIB, CEF/FIB, interfaces, and routing protocol. It is the core of L3VPN segmentation and VRF-lite.

cards.q: What does a VRF isolate on a router?
cards.a: The RIB (routes), CEF/FIB (forwarding), interface membership, and per-VRF routing protocol processes are all fully isolated.
L3VPNs (MPLS + MP-BGP), VRF-lite (no MPLS needed), per-customer multi-tenant separation, and management or out-of-band (OOB) VRFs.

cards.q: What are RD and RT in VRFs, and why do they matter?
cards.a: RD (route distinguisher) makes prefixes unique for MP-BGP, while RT (route target) controls membership and sharing. In VRF-lite the route targets are optional.

cards.q: What command sequence creates a VRF and binds an interface to it?
cards.a: ip vrf CUST1 with rd 65000:100, then under the interface ip vrf forwarding CUST1 followed by ip address. Per-VRF BGP is configured under router bgp with address-family ipv4 vrf CUST1.

cards.q: What happens when you run ip vrf forwarding on an interface?
cards.a: It binds the interface to the VRF and clears/removes the configured IP address, so you must reapply the IP address afterward.

cards.q: How is VRF isolation expressed in the cloud?
cards.a: A cloud VPC or tenant network is the equivalent of a VRF: per-tenant routing tables and fully isolated per-network routing.
show ip vrf (list and detail), show ip route vrf CUST1, show ip cef vrf CUST1, show bgp vpnv4 vrf CUST1, and ping vrf CUST1 10.0.0.2.

cards.q: You configured a VRF but see no routes. What should you check?
cards.a: Check the routing protocol with show ip route vrf, verify the interface binding with show ip vrf, and ensure you ping with the right VRF using ping vrf.

cards.q: How do RD and RT differ in MPLS VPNs?
cards.a: RD provides identity/uniqueness in MP-BGP; RT defines membership and policy (who shares). Getting RT wrong causes wrong route sharing, and an RD overlap breaks uniqueness.

cards.q: Match the quick review: isolates, use, RD, RT, bind, cloud, lite, ping.
cards.a: Isolates RIB/FIB; use = VPN/lite; RD = uniqueness; RT = membership; bind = ip vrf forwarding; cloud = VPC; lite = no MPLS; ping = ping vrf.
